title: Moonshot AI Ordered Kimi Influencers to Hide Paid Partnership Labels in Leaked Brief
summary:
Social media influencers were told to mask paid endorsements in a promotional briefing for Moonshot AI's Kimi K3.1 Pro model. The leaked internal document required creators to submit their drafts for company approval before publishing and explicitly instructed them to avoid using paid partnership labels, a practice that violates X's user rules. The brief also advised creators against tagging the official Kimi account or including links to the company's website.

The briefing supplied specific talking points for creators to push, including claims that Kimi was five times cheaper than Opus 5.5 and that Chinese open-source models have narrowed the performance gap with US frontier models to one month. The disclosure has led to criticism from some AI researchers and prompted discussions on Reddit regarding the U.S. Federal Trade Commission's requirements for advertising disclosure.

selectedTweets.bestBit: 文件还明确写着：不要添加Paid Partnership（付费合作）标识（这是违反X用户规则的）
selectedTweets.text:
Kimi这次在海外真的翻车了。。。

@Kimi_Moonshot 的 K3.1 Pro刚刚发布，结果一位海外AI博主 @elshayib_  直接把疑似Kimi官方提供的网红营销文件给曝光了。

根据他披露的文件，Kimi要求合作创作者在发布内容之前，先把稿件交给他们审核，得到批准后才能发布。

更离谱的是，文件还明确写着：不要添加Paid Partnership（付费合作）标识（这是违反X用户规则的）。

甚至还专门提醒，不需要挂Kimi的官网链接，也不需要@Kimi的官方账号。

与此同时，文件还准备了一整套宣传话术，比如“Kimi就是开源版Opus 5.5，但便宜5倍”“中国把Opus 5.5免费提供给了所有人”“中国开源模型与美国前沿模型的差距已经缩小到一个月”。

这位博主表示，自己拒绝参与这样的宣传，随后还因为批评其他创作者，遭到对方要求删除评论。

事情传到Reddit之后，海外社区也吵起来了。有人直接搬出了美国FTC的广告披露要求，也有人开始质疑这些文件的真实性。

但Kimi K3.1 Pro本身确实是一款值得关注的模型，技术能力也得到了不少认可。

结果现在因为这场营销争议，很多人开始怀疑自己之前看到的那些推荐，到底有多少是真实评价。

一个原本可以靠产品能力获得海外开发者认可的模型，最后却因为营销方式陷入了信任争议。

挺可惜的。

selectedTweets.text:
Kimi K3.1 Pro is genuinely a good model, which makes this even more frustrating. it’s like cheating in a game you’re already good at. 

the leaked campaign briefing apparently tells creators to send their posts for approval and not to disclose the paid partnership.

undisclosed ads are unethical, but they’re also just so damn EASY TO SPOT. and stupid. no good ever comes out of it.

I’ve NEVER taken a single cent for an undisclosed ad, from Kimi or anyone else, and didn’t receive any briefings either. only an early access (like 2 hours before launch!) to test the model and benchmark it.

for transparency, I did have a contact on Kimi’s team who’d occasionally send me updates they thought I’d find interesting, API credits to test their models (which I have mostly used to benchmark CrusaderBench), or even merch. but never money.

this was all in good faith and no different from how I communicate with other AI labs that want me to try what they’re building and share my honest opinions.

but after seeing this, I’ll be ending that relationship until Moonshot apologizes for this.

the researchers and engineers working on this model deserve better, and so did the people who freely shared their opinion about it.

selectedTweets.text:
WTF. This is genuinely shameful and disturbing. A creator has exposed "Moonshot AI's Kimi K3.1 promotional brief". Under 'Narratives You Can Consider,' it suggests claiming that 'China just made Opus 5.5 free to use for everyone,' GPT-6 Sol is 'no comparison,' and Chinese open-source models are just ONE MONTH behind US frontier models. It even invokes US chip restrictions to sell the narrative.

Now look at this GTA demo claiming Kimi built it for $51.98 versus over $500 for Astra/Opus 5.5. That's strikingly similar to the campaign's cost-comparison pitch. I've watched demos from creators I trust, like Bijan Bowen, and the model doesn't look nearly as GOOD as advertised. At this point, how can anyone distinguish independent reviews from paid marketing?
